chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, said:

A group from the people of the outlying regions among the Shiʿah sought permission to enter upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). So he permitted them, and they entered. Then they asked him, in a single session, about thirty thousand issues, and he (عليه السلام) answered, while he was ten years old.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the Imam being addressed in the report
key_terms.الشِّيعَةِ: the Shiʿah, the followers and adherents of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.مَجْلِسٍ: a single sitting or session of gathering
key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٍ: a question or issue requiring an answer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the knowledge of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) at a young age?
ai.summary: This report describes a gathering in which a group of Shiʿah came to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) and asked him an enormous number of questions in one sitting. It highlights his extraordinary knowledge and serves as a biographical indication of his Imam-ordained authority despite his young age.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father who said,

‘I sought permission upon Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) for a group from the people of the suburbs, from the Shias. So he<sup>asws</sup> permitted for them, and they came over and they asked him<sup>asws</sup> in one session, thirty thousand questions. So he<sup>asws</sup> answered, and for him<sup>asws</sup> were ten years (age)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Hashimi from Ali ibn Muhammad or Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hashimi who has said the following “

I went tot see abu Ja‘far (a.s.) in the morning of his marriage to the daughter of al-Ma’al-Ma’mun. The night before I had taken medicine and I was the first to meet him that morning. I was thirsty but did not like to ask for water. Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) looked at me and said, “I think you are thirsty.” I said, “Yes, I am thirsty.” He called, “O Ghulam (male slave or servant) or Jariya (female slave orservant) bring us water.” I said to myself, “They may poison the water. For this reason I became depressed. The servant then came with water. He (abu Ja‘far (a.s.) looked at me with a smile and, “O Ghulam, give the water.” He drank from it and gave the rest to me and I drank. I became thirsty again and did not like to ask for water. He then did as he had done before. When the Ghulam (servant) came with the bowl of water I thought as I thought before. He then took the bowl, drank from it and gave the rest to me with a smile.” Muhammad ibn Hamza has said that this Hashimi told me, “I think what they (Shi‘a ) say (that Imams possess Divine Authority) about him is true.”
